title: Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 now available on AI Gateway for free
description: Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 from InclusionAI is now available on AI Gateway , free until November 3, 2026. The updated model is designed for coding, multi-step reasoning, and agents that use tools. Its 1M-token context window supports workflows involving long documents, code, and extended task histories. Use inclusionai/ling-3.1-flash-1019 as the model name: Free requests still appear in your spend dashboard with a full request trace, they just cost nothing. On November 3, requests will begin charging at the published rate. To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select inclusionai/ling-3.1-flash-1019 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. You can also try Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: Add liveness checks to your Daemons
description: Vercel Daemons now support configuring HTTP liveness checks. Start with an HTTP endpoint in your daemon that reports its health. Keep it lightweight so it responds quickly, and have it return an error status when the daemon is no longer healthy: The daemon configuration now accepts a livenessProbe value pointing at that endpoint: Vercel periodically requests the endpoint and restarts the daemon's container when the check fails, catching a daemon that is still running but no longer healthy. Read the Daemon documentation for more information about liveness checks, including default values and the optional tuning fields. Read more

title: Vercel Flags starts 7x faster and no longer extends function duration
description: On Vercel, the Vercel Flags SDK now initializes faster on cold starts, and usage reporting no longer keeps functions running after the response. Faster cold starts Two changes speed up SDK initialization on cold starts: The SDK loads and parses the flags datafile bundled with your deployment as soon as the client is created, so it’s ready before your code evaluates its first flag. Every function invocation now includes the current datafile revision, so the SDK can check whether the bundled datafile is up to date without a network request. In internal testing, eliminating the network wait reduced p75 cold-start SDK initialization time from over 70 ms to 10 ms, roughly 7x faster. After initialization, flag reads are effectively instant. Across cold and warm invocations, p99 flag-read latency is under 1 ms. Usage reporting no longer extends function duration The SDK previously used waitUntil for usage reporting, keeping functions running after the response was sent. It now passes usage events to the Vercel runtime, so reporting no longer adds to function duration. Update @flags-sdk/vercel to version 1.5.3 or later and redeploy your application: Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation . Read more

title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
description: The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s HarnessAgent now uses libfx , the TypeScript library for fx. The harness and model requests run in your application’s process, while built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox. This simplifies sandbox setup: you no longer need to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host, outside the environment where the agent runs commands. The rewrite also adds: Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running Structured output: generate responses that match a schema Image tool results: return images to the model through toModelOutput() Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process. Update @ai-sdk/harness-fx to the latest version to use the new adapter. Learn more in the fx harness documentation . Read more

title: Node.js 26 LTS is now Generally Available on Vercel
description: Node.js 26 LTS is now Generally Available for builds and Vercel Functions . This release includes: HTTP/2 by default for built-in fetch ( Undici 8 ) lets multiple requests share a connection with servers that support it. This can reduce latency when your functions call APIs or databases over HTTP. Temporal API offers an alternative to Date with immutable values and built-in time zone and calendar support. V8 version 14.6 , the updated JavaScript engine, adds features such as Map.prototype.getOrInsert() to retrieve an existing value or insert a default when a key is missing. Using Node.js 26 Node.js 26 is the default for all new projects. Automatic upgrades: If engines.node in your existing project’s package.json allows 26, such as >=20 , your Node.js builds on Vercel will use 26 on the next deployment. Manual upgrades: Set engines.node to 26.x in your project's package.json and redeploy. Prebuilt deployments: Use Vercel CLI version 65.8.0 or later to deploy Node.js 26 Functions. HTTP/1.1 in Functions: To keep HTTP/1.1, set the VERCEL_FETCH_DISABLE_H2 environment variable to 1 and redeploy. Minor and patch updates to Node.js 26 roll out automatically for builds and Vercel Functions. Read the Node.js version documentation to learn more. Read more

title: Vercel Connect adds webhook triggers for more providers
description: Vercel Connect now supports webhook triggers for Resend , X , Twilio , Notion , and Telegram . Connect receives webhook events, such as Telegram bot messages or emails received by your Resend domain, and forwards them to an endpoint in your Vercel project. It verifies incoming requests and handles provider heartbeats and verification challenges for you. To get started: Open Vercel Connect in the dashboard. Enable triggers when creating a connector for your provider or in an existing connector’s settings. Connect registers webhooks automatically for Resend and Telegram. For Twilio, Notion, and X, use the webhook URL from Connect and follow its instructions to complete setup in the provider’s settings. Add a trigger destination to choose the project and endpoint that should receive events. You can turn triggers on or off later in the connector’s settings. In the connector’s Observability tab, select Live to watch incoming trigger events. These connectors join existing trigger support for Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, and Linear. Learn more in the Connect triggers documentation . Read more

title: Control AI crawlers and assistants separately in Vercel Firewall
description: You can now log or block requests from AI crawlers and AI assistants separately with the AI Bots managed ruleset in Vercel Firewall . AI crawlers: bots that collect content for indexing and model training AI assistants: bots that fetch pages in response to user actions or search queries For example, you can block AI crawlers while allowing AI assistants to retrieve your content to answer users’ questions. Vercel updates the rules as new bots are added. To configure these controls, open your project’s Security > Firewall > Rules . Under Bot Management , enable AI Bots and select the gear icon beside it. Set an action for AI crawlers and AI assistants, then review and publish your changes. You can also modify these rule settings using the Vercel CLI: type: embedded-entry-inline id: 30azXU4HVTfrsO9MbBOCLv Review the changes with vercel firewall diff , then apply them with vercel firewall publish . The AI Bots managed ruleset is available on all plans. Learn more in the documentation . Read more

title: Mistral Large 4 updated weights and lower pricing on AI Gateway
description: Mistral Large 4 from Mistral now uses updated weights on AI Gateway , with lower pricing for input, cached input, and output tokens. According to Mistral’s release announcement , the updated weights improve agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity, with greater token efficiency on coding tasks. The release also improves spreadsheet creation and editing, web research, and resistance to prompt injection. If you were already using mistral/mistral-large-4 via AI Gateway, there is no need to change your model to start using the updated version. The existing model ID string uses the new model with updated weights and pricing.
